Text: "Kirron Kher, BJP’s Chandigarh MP, said “Rape is part of Indian culture and tradition. We cannot stop it!”"
Claim author: Saqib Ghias Khan
Claim date: October 10, 2020
Claim origin: https://www.facebook.com/saqibkhan2767/posts/3408050572635173
before_justification: The claim is refuted because investigations by fact-checkers, including [Factly.in](https://factly.in/kirron-kher-did-not-say-that-rapes-cannot-be-stopped/) and [The Logical Indian](https://thelogicalindian.com/tags/kirron-kher), found that the quote attributed to Kirron Kher was a distortion of her actual words. During a 2017 press conference, Kher stated that "such incidents have been taking place since forever" but emphasized that change is possible through a shift in mindset and family values, a position misrepresented in the viral claim. No verifiable record supports the alleged statement, and mainstream reporting treated it as a social media misrepresentation.
after_justification: The claim is refuted because a reputable fact-checking organization, [Factly](https://factly.in/kirron-kher-did-not-say-that-rapes-cannot-be-stopped/), investigated and found it false, stating that Kirron Kher's words were twisted. The alleged quote lacks a verifiable primary source and appears to have been taken out of context.

adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text:
An image with Kirron Kher’s quote on rapes is being shared by many users with the claim that she said rapes are part of the tradition and cannot be stopped.
Claim: Kirron Kher: “Rapes are happening from ages, it is part of the tradition, we cannot stop them.”
Fact: Kirron Kher did not say that rapes are part of the tradition and cannot be stopped. Her words were twisted to claim that she made the above statements.
She said that rapes can be stopped by changing the mindset of the people. Hence the claim made in the post is FALSE.
When searched for the statements made by Kirron Kher on rapes, an article published by ANI can be found in the search results.
According to the article, Kirron Kher said, ‘Such incidents have been taking place since forever. Only change in the mindset can bring about a change.
Change in society starts from within a family”. Her statements on rapes in Haryana can be watched in a video uploaded by Times of India in January 2018.
She did not say that rapes are part of the tradition and cannot be stopped. But she said that rapes can be stopped by changing the mindset of people and by giving equal status to women in the family.
To sum it up, Kirron Kher did not say that rapes cannot be stopped.

The actor-turned-politician gave BJP its first win in 16 years when she defeated four-time MP and former railway minister Pawan Kumar Bansal, spawning hope that the city would see massive development and change.

Recently, her own party leader and former union minister Harmohan Dhawan said BJP has betrayed residents by not fulfilling a single promise they made in the manifesto before the 2014 Lok Sabha elections.

She has also failed to regularise need-based changes in Chandigarh Housing Board units or come up with a housing scheme for UT employees.
Promises such as construction of a film city, setting up of a single window system, and abolition of contractual labour are also gathering dust.

She carved out a niche for herself in the Bollywood with her fine acting skills. Kirron Kher made her film debut in 1983 in the Punjabi feature Aasra Pyar Da.
She has played various roles in Bengali, Malayalam, Hindi and English cinema. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has again placed its trust in her, fielding her from Chandigarh against Congress veteran Pawan Bansal.
Kirron had defeated Bansal in 2014 by a margin of around 70,000 votes.
She courted criticism from the Congress for using the word “railgate” in a poster proposing monorail over metro.
The poster read, “because Kirron Kher is not interested in Railgate – vote for honesty not corruption.”
The Congress filed a complaint with the Election Commission, saying, “The word Railgate is maliciously used to defame former Union Minister Pawan Kumar Bansal, though he has been given clean chit by relevant investigative agencies in the alleged case.”
The Railgate scam was linked to Bansal's nephew. However, the actor-politician denied the charges.

She graduated from the Department of Indian Theatre of Panjab University, Chandigarh. She is married to seasoned film actor Anupam Kher.
She joined the BJP in 2009. She campaigned for the saffron party across the country in the 2009 general elections and in Chandigarh Municipal Corporation polls.

A BJP Member of Parliament from Chandigarh since 2014, Kirron Kher is a well-known figure in politics as well as in Hindi cinema.
Kirron, who is married to actor Anupam Kher, joined the BJP in 2009 and was elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2012.
Kher was first elected to the Lok Sabha in 2014 by defeating Congress stalwart Pawan Bansal and Aam Aadmi Party’s candidate and celebrity Gul Panag.
Riding on the Modi wave, she again defeated Bansal in the 2019 parliamentary polls.
Born in Amritsar in 1955, Kirron studied at the National School of Drama in New Delhi and began her acting career in theatre.
She made her film debut in 1983 with the film "Aasmaan Se Aa Gaya". She went on to star in a number of successful films, including "Devdas" (2002), "Rang De Basanti" (2006), and "Main Hoon Na" (2004).
Kher is a recipient of numerous awards, including the National Film Award for Best Actress, the National Film Award – Special Jury Award, the IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actress, the Guild Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role, and the Indian Telly Award for Best Judge Panel.
Known for her outspoken nature, Kher, 68, drew flak for her comments during a political address in her constituency Chandigarh in March 2023.
She used phrases such as “laanat hai” and “chhittar ferne chahiye” while referring to voters. She was speaking about the development work she had done for the residents of Deep Complex in Chandigarh.
During her speech, Kher stated, “Agar Deep Complex mein mujhe ek bhi banda vote na dale, to badi laanat ki baat hai.
Jaakar chhittar ferne chahiye unko (If no one from Deep Complex votes for me, it will be a highly shameful thing.
This was not the first time that she has faced criticism for her use of language. In June 2022, Kher had referred to AAP councillors as “dunger” (animals) during a press conference.
She had criticised their conduct at the first House meeting of Chandigarh stating, “They were breaking tables and glasses.

An image with Kirron Kher’s quote on rapes is being shared by many users with the claim that she said rapes are part of the tradition and cannot be stopped.
Claim: Kirron Kher: “Rapes are happening from ages, it is part of the tradition, we cannot stop them.”
Fact: Kirron Kher did not say that rapes are part of the tradition and cannot be stopped. Her words were twisted to claim that she made the above statements.
She said that rapes can be stopped by changing the mindset of the people. Hence the claim made in the post is FALSE.
When searched for the statements made by Kirron Kher on rapes, an article published by ANI can be found in the search results.
According to the article, Kirron Kher said, ‘Such incidents have been taking place since forever. Only change in the mindset can bring about a change.
Change in society starts from within a family”. Her statements on rapes in Haryana can be watched in a video uploaded by Times of India in January 2018.
She did not say that rapes are part of the tradition and cannot be stopped. But she said that rapes can be stopped by changing the mindset of people and by giving equal status to women in the family.
To sum it up, Kirron Kher did not say that rapes cannot be stopped.

retrieved_evidence.text:
New Delhi: Bollywood actor Anupam Kher came under fire on social media for quoting Sikh spiritual leader Guru Gobind Singh to praise BJP leader Sambit Patra in a tweet Wednesday, which has since been deleted.
The line “sava lakh se ek bhida dun” is one of the most famous and sacred Sikh war cries coined by Guru Gobind Singh during the Second War of Chamkaur Sahib against the Mughals in 1705.
Kher tagged BJP national spokesperson Patra after the party leader faced scathing criticism for tweeting the viral photograph of a three-year-old boy sitting on his grandfather’s corpse, who was killed in the crossfire between militants and security personnel in Jammu and Kashmir’s Sopore, with the caption “PULITZER LOVERS??”.
Soon after, Kher faced immense backlash for using the sacred quote and for hurting the sentiments of the Sikh community.
He then deleted the tweet and issued an apology Thursday.
“In one of my previous tweets, I wrote something wrong. I apologise for that,” he said.

Several Congress leaders were among those that lashed out at Kher, who is married to BJP MP Kirron Kher, for his ‘insensitive’ tweet.
Congress MP Ravneet Singh Bittu from Punjab, said, “How dare @AnupamPKher uses sacred words of Guru Gobind Singh ji to describe the spokesperson of BJP.
It spoils the martial image of Sikhs. It is a bid of RSS to dilute strong tenets of Sikhism. PM Modi should tender an immediate apology and kick out Kher and his wife from bjp.”
Punjab cabinet minister and Congress leader Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa also called on the Akal Takht Jathedar to intervene in the matter.
